To win a game, a player must score at least 11 points and lead by at least two. At 10–10, play continues. A score of 11–10 is insufficient, but 12–10 wins the game.
A match is the best of an agreed odd number of games. In a best-of-three match, for example, the first player to win two games wins the match.

A draw determines who gets first choice of serving, receiving, or end of the table. The other player chooses from the options left. The first receiver of one game serves first in the next.
Each player normally serves for two consecutive rallies. At 10–10, service alternates after every point until the game ends.
serve service palm toss height 16 cm vertical hidden visible spin bounce

Start with the ball resting on an open, still palm. Toss it nearly vertically without spin so it rises at least 16 cm, then strike it as it falls. Until it is struck, the ball must stay above the playing surface, behind the end line, and visible to the receiver.
The ball must bounce first on the side of the server and then on the side of the receiver. A singles serve may go to either half of the opposing court.
net let re-serve replay interruption receiver not ready interference
The ball touches the net on service

Replay a serve that touches the net assembly if the serve is otherwise legal. If the ball touches the net and misses the receiving court, it is a service fault. During a rally, a return may touch the net and still be legal if it lands on the opposing court.
The rally is a let if the receiver was not ready and made no attempt to strike the ball. Play may also be stopped and replayed because of outside interference.
out edge side table hand double hit racket paddle volley ball point contact
A player wins the point if the opponent serves incorrectly or fails to return the ball to the opposing playing surface. Deliberately striking the ball twice in succession also loses the point.
A ball that touches the top edge is in. The vertical side of the table is outside the playing surface.
A player loses the point if, during a rally, they touch the playing surface with their free hand, move the table, or touch the net assembly.
swap sides change ends deciding final last game five 5 points
After each game, players switch to opposite ends of the table.
In the last possible game of a match, players change ends when either player first reaches five points. Tap “Swap sides” on the scoreboard to move the panels while preserving the score and server.
pairs two versus two diagonal right court partner receive order alternating
In doubles, the ball must bounce in the right half-court of the serving pair and then in the right half-court of the receiving pair.

After service and receive, partners alternate returns. When service changes, the previous receiver serves and the previous server’s partner receives. In the deciding game, the pair due to receive next changes its receiving order when either pair first reaches five points.
